note: The English teen edition quotes the ESV (WEB for Proverbs 13:15) in each chapter's epigraph. Every epigraph is instead the full verse from Louis Segond 1910 — the register the shipped French corpus uses — pasted verbatim from the fra_lsg USFM text, with the version label dropped. `mined` rows are exact substrings of the cited shipped *.fr.json; a `self_rendered` epigraph here is still verbatim Segond, just not yet attested in the corpus (Matthew 6:20 is in men-and-women-who-gave-everything-2.fr with a lower-case « mais »; the epigraph capitalises it). Matthew 10:37 is attested only in grace-for-grace-2.fr, a copyright-blocked edition, so it is not cited.

Psalm numbering: the epigraphs display Segond's verse numbers (« Psaume 81:11 », « Psaume 68:6 »), which are 81:10 and 68:5 in the English numbering used for the references here. Segond's Psalm 81 has no « toute grande » for “wide”; the quoted verse keeps Segond, and the chapter title / narration carry the idea (« Ouvre grand ta bouche »).

In-body allusions quoted as Segond fragments: 2 Corinthians 9:7b, 2 Chronicles 32:8a, Matthew 6:11, Psalm 81:10b, Zechariah 4:6b, Romans 13:8a. Müller's own words (from his Narrative, quoted in English in the source) are rendered fresh in French, not from a published French Narrative. Egress to api.takeroot.bible was not used.
